verdict.rationale: ByteAsk documents its own live-debugging capability: it joins a gdb session through a bridge, reads live state, asks before changing anything, and returns frames, files and line numbers. However, it is positioned as a C/C++ agent, and nothing shows it debugging a running web application specifically, such as browser or front-end state, HTTP requests, or web runtimes. missing for 10: evidence of debugging live web applications (browser/web runtime, network or request inspection), documentation of attaching to a running web server process, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug a live running web application directly from my coding assistant

citations.quote: ByteAsk joins through a bridge you start in your gdb, reads the live state, and asks before it changes anything.
It hands back the raw report with the frames, files and line numbers intact
drives the real toolchain - sanitizers, your test suite, and any gdb session you already have open
